Open Start and type your company name and your limits in the yellow cells: host agency rate, advisor rate, chase days, escalation days, grace days, smallest claim and the share you want to keep.
Check Team, Suppliers, Trips and Bookings. They hold the people, the supplier commission rates and terms, and every booking a commission can come from.
Add a row on Commissions for each booking that earns commission: expected amount and date. Received amount, received date and status are filled in when the supplier pays.
Read Commissions every week: days overdue, ageing band and next step show what to chase, wait for or escalate.
Record every chase on Chase Log with the answer and the promised date. Broken promises and slow answers are flagged for you.
Use Short-pay Claims, Clawbacks and Rate History to catch short payments, commissions taken back and supplier rate changes.
Type the host agency statement on Host Statements each month and compare it with what you recorded. Keep your yearly sales next to Host Tiers.
Run Advisor Payouts each month: agency share, advisor rate, payout, year to date and what is still owed.
Watch Commission Forecast, Supplier Pay Calendar and Unclaimed Commissions for what is coming and what must be claimed.
Track Supplier Bonuses against each sales target and Service Fees with their payment status.
Read Commission by Category, Ageing and Owner Net Earnings for the monthly picture and what the business keeps.
Use the 14 calculators for commission splits, net earnings per trip, ageing, chase priority, short-pay checks, escalation, host tiers, payouts, forecasts, clawbacks, quotes, bonuses and what-ifs.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in. Read the Commission Dashboard and Charts every week.

Clients with trips, sales, last trip and loyalty tier
One row per client: kind, interest, source, advisor and tier; trips, sales, lifetime value, last trip, days since the trip and touch, and the repeat, lapse, contact and tier checks fill in.
Trips with price per person and gaps between trips
One row per trip: client, type, destination, dates, advisor, price, commission and fee; price per person, repeat booking and the days since the client last travelled fill in by themselves.
Client profiles with travel style and nights travelled
One row per client profile: travel style, pace, budget level, usual group size and dislikes; the trips taken, nights travelled, spend per night and the age of the profile fill in by themselves.
Travel preferences by kind with the date they were noted
One row per preference: kind (seat, room, meal, activity, hotel, transport, pace), the value and a note; the days since it was noted and the preferences held for the client fill in.
Companions with passport expiry and dietary needs
One row per person who usually travels with a client: relation, age band, passport expiry and dietary need; the days to expiry and the passport check fill in by themselves.
Special dates with days to the next one
One row per birthday, anniversary, school holiday or other date a client cares about; the next date, the days to it, the age or years it marks and the loyalty tier fill in by themselves.
Touchpoints with channel, topic and next touch
One row per contact with a client: date, channel, topic, advisor and the next touch date; the days since the touch and the follow-up check fill in by themselves.
Loyalty tiers with trips and sales needed
One row per tier: the trips taken or the sales that earn it; a client takes the higher of the two. Change the numbers and every client earned tier follows.
Referrals with the value each one brought
One row per client who came by recommendation: who referred them, the date, the first trip and whether a thank-you went out; the trips, sales and commission they brought fill in by themselves.
Reviews with rating, source and reply check
One row per review: the trip, rating, source and comment; the stars as a number, the destination and the check that a low rating needs a reply fill in by themselves.
Past trip ideas with years waiting
One row per wish a client has mentioned: the wish, the destination and the year they hope to go; the years waiting, the interest and whether they have been there already fill in by themselves.
Win-back list with months since the last trip
One row per client who has not travelled for a long time: reason, offer and status; the last trip, months since it, past spend, tier and the wait check fill in by themselves.
One row per note about a client: date, advisor, the note and an optional follow-up date; the days to follow up and the follow-up check fill in by themselves.
Passport and visa watch against the trip dates
One row per traveller and document: the expiry and the trip that needs it; the days to expiry, the days valid after the trip and the risk check fill in. Check the destination current rules.
Birthday and anniversary offers with sent date and result
One row per offer for a special date: the date, the offer, when it was sent and the result; the days to the date and the check that an offer is sent, due or planned fill in by themselves.
Client segments with clients, sales and average value
One row per segment: the client kind and the trips and sales a client needs; the clients in it, their sales, the average value and the share of all sales fill in by themselves.
Newsletter list with topics and last opened
One row per client on the newsletter: the opt-in date, topics and whether they still subscribe; the months subscribed and the check for subscribers who stopped opening fill in by themselves.
Anniversary trips due with the original trip
One row per client with a trip anniversary coming: the original trip, the date and the idea; the destination, the original price, the years and the days to it fill in by themselves.
Advisors and freelance specialists with their clients
One row per team member with phone and share of the commission; the clients each advisor looks after, the active ones, their sales and the clients overdue for contact fill in by themselves.
Clients by month with repeat share and reviews
One row per month: the month is typed, and the new clients, bookings, repeat bookings, repeat share, reviews, average rating and touches fill in from the other sheets.
